newsitem.title: USA: CBOT wheat ends down despite strong delivery stops.
newsitem.headline: CBOT wheat ends down despite strong delivery stops.

text.p: CBOT wheat futures closed lower on a technical setback after recent gains, despite strong stopping of the deliveries posted Thursday against the December contract, traders said.
The lower close also defied wheat export sales numbers that traders considered satisfactory.
"The wheat numbers were okay but it has had a decent rally lately so it set back," said Ron Kucha of O'Connor and Co.
The December contract expired quietly at 1201 CST, up one cent at $4.03 per bushel. December surged roughly 12 cents per bushel to a session high of $4.14 in early dealings.
Traders said the early rally was triggered when a speculative short scrambled to get out of the market.
"Whoever was short in there got very nervous because Dreyfus stopped all the wheat," a trader said.
Term Commodities, the marketing arm of Louis Dreyfus Corp, stopped 715,000 bushels of the 815,000 posted Thursday for delivery on the December contract, according to the CBOT.
Wheat closed 1/2 to 6-1/4 cents per bushel lower, with March down 1/2 at $4.00-1/4.

Wheat was boosted by a strong number in USDA's weekly export sales report. USDA Thursday said U.S. net export sales of wheat during the week ended December 12 totaled 349,300 tonnes, midrange of trade expectations for 300,000 to 400,000 tonnes.
There also was talk that wheat was supported by cold weather in the U.S. winter wheat growing region which was leading to some fears portions of the crop would be harmed.
The market took note of news Argentina raised its estimate for its wheat crop to 15.2 million tonnes from the previous 14.9 million.
But Argentine Agriculture Secretary Felipe Sola said that about one million tonnes of the crop had quality problems and will probably be sold as forage grain.

Cargill Inc bought 1.5 million bushels of March and Dean Witter Reynolds bought 2.5 million bushels of March, traders said. Refco Inc, Rand Financial, Term Commodities and Produce Grain each sold one million bushels of March, they said.
Wheat futures volume was estimated at 15,000 contracts, below the 32,691 traded Wednesday, according to the CBOT.
In wheat options, Tenco Inc bought 200 March $4.30 calls at 7-1/4 to 8 cents, bought 200 March $4.20 calls at 10 cents and Refco Inc bought 200 March $3.90 puts at 10-3/4 to 11 cents, traders said.
Wheat options volume was estimated at 8,000 contracts, below the 14,046 traded Wednesday.
